context.description: Yorke Peninsula is a farming peninsula between Gulf St Vincent and Spencer Gulf, ringed by small coastal towns with long jetties. Ardrossan sits on top of red clay cliffs, Edithburgh has a tidal swimming pool and Wool Bay a jetty and lime kilns, and Port Victoria keeps a maritime museum. Corny Point Lighthouse looks over the far southwest, and an 1855 lighthouse stands on Troubridge Island offshore from Edithburgh.

context.description: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park covers the south-western tip of Yorke Peninsula, about 300 km by road from Adelaide, and is managed jointly with the Narungga traditional owners. The Ethel ran aground here in 1904, and its remains still lie on the beach beside the lighthouse at Cape Spencer. Trails run from 30-minute strolls to four-hour hikes, through heath and mallee to the cliff tops. The park's beaches draw campers, anglers and surfers, and its abandoned gypsum township of Inneston has walking trails and restored cottages.
